ENGAGEMENTS / A CLEAR FIRST STEP

One workflow.
A defined way forward.

Choose the stage that matches your project. Every paid engagement starts with a written scope, agreed inputs, and a review point.

01 / DISCOVERY

Check feasibility.

For a problem that needs a clearer technical plan.

  • Review the current workflow and sample inputs
  • Identify data, access, and integration needs
  • Define success criteria and the proposed next step

Proposed output: a scoped brief and evaluation plan.

02 / FIXED-SCOPE PILOT

Build and evaluate.

For one use case with available inputs and a clear finish line.

  • Implement the agreed component or interface
  • Review representative examples and failure cases
  • Decide whether to extend, revise, or hand over

Proposed output: a working pilot and evaluation notes.

Scope a pilot ↗
03 / INTEGRATION

Fit the workflow.

For a defined component that needs to connect to your existing application.

  • Agree APIs, access, and deployment boundaries
  • Document configuration and operational requirements
  • Review source handover and any support arrangement

Proposed output: the scoped integration and handover.

PRICING AND DELIVERY

A quote that reflects
the actual work.

Data quality, integrations, access controls, and evaluation requirements determine the effort. After reviewing your brief, we agree the deliverables, milestones, price, and payment terms in writing.

Implementation

The engineering work and agreed revision scope are priced in the proposal.

Running costs

Changes and support

BEFORE YOU START

Clear answers.
A better brief.

How much will a project cost?+

The quote follows a review of the use case, available data, integrations, and evaluation requirements. The written proposal separates implementation from model usage, hosting, and ongoing support.

How long does a pilot take?+

The schedule is agreed after reviewing the inputs and access requirements. The proposal sets milestones, review points, and dependencies so the delivery plan reflects the actual work.

What do you need from us?+

Start with a workflow description, a few non-sensitive examples, and what a useful result would look like. Access to private data is agreed separately before it is shared.

How will we judge the result?+

We agree representative test inputs and acceptance criteria before development. The review covers useful results, failure cases, and the limits of the implementation.

What do we receive at handover?+

The written scope defines the agreed code, setup instructions, evaluation notes, and walkthrough. Hosting accounts, third-party dependencies, ownership terms, and any support period are made explicit.

Can you work with another agency?+

Yes. A bounded implementation partnership can fit an agency project. We agree who owns client communication, code, delivery, and support before work starts.
